creator: huberman

promoted.note: min_k is 15 here, NOT the 6 tune.py derived below -- 6 was tested directly (chain_deploy100_k6_recheck.json, 46/100 failing) and measured worse than 15 (41/100), because tune.py optimises for recall-at-cheapest-pool and this archive's concentration in one dominant video makes a wider net net-beneficial despite more noise. min_k=15/expand=2 were themselves first borrowed from healthygamer's BASELINES.md, not derived, then kept because the derived k=6 measured worse, not because 15 was independently re-validated as optimal. k=10 was the untried middle ground; see still_open for the result once chain-scored.
promoted.what_this_fixed: --commit was never turned on in any earlier run. Forcing the controller to name specific passages before writing, then rebuilding context to show only those, cut failures from 41/100 (k=15, no commit) to 38/100 -- the only lever tried that improved both ungrounded AND padding together rather than trading one for the other. Also ~23% faster (22.9s vs 29.7s mean), not slower, because the final answer-writing turn sees a much smaller context.
what_did_not_help: retrieving via properly re-derived k=6 instead of borrowed k=15: worse (46/100)
re-enabling the in-loop judge + 1 retry: flat (40/99), traded ungrounded for padding
instructing the controller that a short answer is fine when material is thin: flat (42/99), traded ungrounded for padding
stacking the thin-material instruction on top of --commit: worse than commit alone (41/100)

a comprehensive instruction naming four specific editorializing/generalizing patterns (built from real judge reasoning), stacked on --commit: worse than commit alone (45/100) -- confirms proto/RECIPE.md's own dead end ('asking the model not to invent joins... tried twice, lost twice') a third time

min_k=10 (the untried middle ground) combined with --commit: decisively worse, not a close call -- 70/100 failing against 34/100 for min_k=15 under the same scoring (work/huberman/reports/chain_deploy100_commit_k10.json). Mean committed pool dropped from 85.5 to 67.7 passages/question, and context_utilization collapsed from 0.818 to 0.247, context_recall from 0.938 to 0.699 -- a narrower floor gives the controller less to commit to, and --commit has nothing to recover once the right passage was never retrieved. min_k=15 stays promoted.
still_open: the dominant residual failure (ungrounded, 26%) is the controller adding its own evaluation/generalization/inference/extension on top of real facts -- consistent across every config tried, not fixed by any instruction attempt

the failing_any_measure count quoted above (38) and the count recomputed later with compare.py's own fails() thresholds (34) disagree by 4 questions -- the script that produced the original 38 was an ad hoc one-liner, not saved. compare.py's fails() (faithfulness<0.85, context_recall<0.50, context_utilization<0.25, relevancy<0.70) is the only threshold definition that actually exists in the repo; treat 34 as the figure backed by checked-in code, 38 as the number this file was first measured and promoted against. Both agree min_k=15+commit is the best arm found.

style-pairs' oracle-answer generation (the input side of training pairs) uses agent.py's simpler single-call path, NOT harness/loop.py -- this commit fix does not apply there and the 132 pairs already trained on were generated without it

the same --commit fix, tried on healthygamer's own 'narrow' arm (BASELINES.md), showed real gains (faithfulness 0.929->0.978, relevancy 0.845->0.933) but was bundled with a word-cap that caused separate regressions and was never re-isolated -- untested whether commit alone would improve Dr K's own promoted config too
